item.title: Flat-Top Solitons as Acoustic Resonant Cavities
item.description: arXiv:2611.10964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A two-dimensional flat-top soliton forms an acoustic resonator without external confinement. Its nearly uniform interior carries sound, while its moving edge selects a discrete sequence of radial wavelengths. For the cubic--quintic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, we connect this spectrum to bulk compressibility, radius, and line tension. Numerical simulations confirm the predicted resonances below the particle-emission threshold. The soliton itself provides the sound-carrying medium and the moving boundary, allowing its resonance frequencies to be predicted from its stationary properties.
item.dc:creator: M. O. D. Alotaibi, L. Al Sakkaf, U. Al Khawaja

item.title: Axis-switching oscillations of elliptic scroll rings in excitable media
item.description: arXiv:2611.11538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scroll waves in three-dimensional excitable media rotate around a filament that moves according to its local curvature. Using simulations of the Barkley model, we show that initially planar, elliptic scroll rings perform the axis-switching oscillation known from elliptic vortex rings in fluids: while the ring drifts along its axis, it buckles into a saddle, becomes planar again with interchanged axes, and repeats this cycle. The oscillation occurs for vanishing, positive, and negative filament tension. As predicted by a kinematic filament equation, its period scales approximately with the square of the ring radius and inversely with the drift coefficient. For our main model parameters, however, the oscillation is about 1.45 times slower than the linear prediction based on the drift of circular rings of the same size. A curvature-dependent drift coefficient accounts for a factor of about 1.25, while the remaining slowdown results mainly from a weaker coupling of out-of-plane to in-plane deformations, which a fourth-order rigidity term does not describe. In contrast, the Panfilov-Rudenko model and the Atri model of Ca$^{2+}$ waves follow the linear prediction within about 6%, showing that the slowdown depends on the kinetics.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Steinbock

item.title: Turing Instability of a Closed Nutrient-Phytoplankton-Zooplankton-Detritus Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.10221v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Turing instability in a closed Nutrient-Phytoplankton-Zooplankton-Detritus (NPZD) ecosystem model with nutrient recycling, formulated as a reaction-diffusion system without an explicit time-delay. The detritus compartment represents the biomass during the recycling process and acts to introduce a time delay in this process. Total biomass in the system is conserved, leading to a closed model. Although spatial diffusion typically promotes stability, our focus is on understanding how different diffusion rates for different species can destabilize steady states and give rise to spatial patterns. To address this, we first perform linear stability analysis to identify conditions under which Turing instability may occur. We then validate these theoretical predictions through numerical simulations. Our approach develops both intuition and rigorous analysis of how diffusion influences instabilities in the context of a conservative system, offering a comprehensive framework for understanding pattern formation in multi-species plankton ecosystems.
item.dc:creator: Xiangye Xu, Sue Ann Campbell, Francis J. Poulin

item.title: Self-organization of magnetic islands and zonal magnetic fields driven by slab microtearing modes in the absence of magnetic shear
item.description: arXiv:2611.10446v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-organization in collisional microtearing turbulence is investigated using gyrokinetic simulations in a slab geometry without equilibrium magnetic shear. Unlike magnetically driven conventional tearing instabilities, microtearing instabilities are driven by the electron temperature gradient. Electron temperature fluctuations are found to contain most of the gyrokinetic free energy. Although magnetic perturbations contribute little to the free energy, the magnetic field structure plays a crucial role in the nonlinear evolution of microtearing turbulence. Zonal magnetic fields emerge spontaneously through the nonlinear interaction between magnetic perturbations and electron temperature fluctuations. These zonal fields provide an effective magnetic shear that enables magnetic islands to form despite the absence of equilibrium magnetic shear. The electron temperature profile is flattened within the islands. This flattening reduces the instability drive and is expected to promote turbulence saturation.
item.dc:creator: Mitsuyoshi Yagyu, Ryusuke Numata, Seiya Nishimura

item.title: Relative Entropy Methods for Rotating Stars in the Compressible Euler-Riesz Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.11059v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish finite-time relative entropy estimates for axisymmetric finite-energy entropy solutions of the three-dimensional attractive compressible Euler-Riesz equations near a prescribed compactly supported rotating star. The entropy solutions are assumed to have the same total mass as the steady state and to satisfy the prescribed angular momentum relation. For general pressure laws, the compatibility with the angular momentum constraint, together with the nonnegative rotational remainder, yields a cancellation of the centrifugal terms. For axisymmetric perturbations, the gradient of the perturbed Riesz potential has no azimuthal component and therefore couples only to those momentum components controlled by the modulated kinetic energy. The density-weighted estimates for the Riesz potential then allow us to close the relative entropy inequality. Under an additional higher-integrability assumption on the density, the result extends to the Chandrasekhar pressure law, yielding a corresponding stability estimate for rotating white dwarf stars.
item.dc:creator: Gui-Qiang G. Chen, Difan Yuan

item.title: Quantum entanglement as a resource for self-organization and stabilization
item.description: arXiv:2611.11175v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can quantum entanglement generate macroscopic order that persists after the entanglement itself disappears? We establish such a mechanism in a driven-dissipative bosonic lattice, where local entanglement enables transport that amplifies spatial fluctuations into extended Turing patterns. For the full nonlinear dynamics with noise and disorder, we derive rigorous finite-time bounds on pattern intensity for all admissible separable evolutions, allowing arbitrary classical correlations. Quantum dynamics produces pattern intensities beyond these bounds during both formation and stabilization under noise. The excess intensity also provides a lower bound on the accumulated transport contribution beyond the separable limit. We further introduce an environment that responds to emerging order by suppressing local coherence and activating classical transport. The patterns then persist as local entanglement is lost, with both stages arising from a single time-independent Lindblad equation. These results show how transient quantum resources can establish persistent macroscopic order, opening new directions for harnessing self-organization in nonequilibrium systems.
item.dc:creator: Kazuki Ikeda

item.title: Thermochemical Rossby waves in rapid rotation: from swallowtail geometry to nonlinear selection
item.description: arXiv:2611.11719v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When heat and solute both destabilise a rapidly rotating fluid, do their buoyancies add? Codensity models assume so, giving a straight onset diagonal; spherical shells show curved and kinked thresholds. We study the Busse--Simitev rotating annulus, whose normal modes obey an exact complex cubic dispersion relation. Combining the Bilharz criterion with the neutral-curve envelope yields, in the rapid-rotation limit, an explicit swallowtail wave front, in Arnold's sense, that bends the codensity diagonal into smooth and then kinked thresholds as the diffusivity ratio decreases. Its cusp edges lie inside the unstable domain and its exposed kink ends at the swallowtail singularity; these are singularities of wave-number selection, without coalescence of temporal eigenvalues, and the swallowtail diffusivity ratio has analytical small- and large-Prandtl-number limits. At a kink, broad, fast thermal and narrow, slow compositional Rossby waves become neutral together; hidden arcs mark the birth and merger of unstable wave-number bands. The same geometry enters nonlinear selection: mean-scalar feedback factors through neutral-arc normals and scalar responses, so the mean-profile coexistence margin vanishes with the kink angle as the waves merge. Complete cubic coefficients predict robust coexistence at a reference corner and a narrow bistable interval near merger. Exact finite-rotation corners and periodic-cell simulations confirm the coexisting waves and their invasion thresholds.
item.dc:creator: Oleg N. Kirillov

item.title: Origin of devil's staircases and anomalous Arnold tongues of breathing solitons in optical Kerr resonators
item.description: arXiv:2611.11804v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Synchronization phenomena are ubiquitous across natural and engineered systems, and optical resonators supporting breathing solitons offer a natural platform for their investigation. In driven Kerr cavities described by the Lugiato-Lefever equation (LLE), breathing-soliton dynamics constitute a minimal setting in which such behavior can be systematically analyzed. Despite recent observations of intricate self-synchronization structures in mode-locked lasers-such as subharmonic entrainment, devil's staircases, and holes within Arnold tongues, i.e., regions of unsynchronized dynamics embedded within synchronized domains-their physical origin has remained elusive due to the complexity of laser dynamics. Here, we demonstrate that these phenomena emerge in the universal framework of the LLE. By reducing the problem to this model, we uncover the mechanism responsible for both the devil's staircase and the formation of holes within Arnold tongues. This provides a unified physical picture of synchronization in nonlinear systems, extending beyond optics and providing insight into analogous predictions and observations in fluids and other oscillatory media. In addition, we identify the regimes of high-order synchronization, enabling the generation of ultradense frequency combs, opening new directions for precision photonic applications.
item.dc:creator: Tianhao Xian, Junsong Peng, Sonia Boscolo, Christophe Finot, Heping Zeng

item.title: Non-Equilibrium Ising-Bloch Transition in Polarization Cavity Solitons
item.description: arXiv:2611.12626v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Polarization cavity solitons in coherently driven Kerr resonators undergo a sequence of dynamical bifurcations as the cavity detuning is increased. Here we show that a stationary localized state containing an Ising wall first becomes a fixed breather and then develops finite chirality and drift motion through a spontaneous non-equilibrium Ising-Bloch transition. Stability analyses identify the modes responsible for the breathing and the motion, revealing controllable dynamics of polarization cavity solitons.
item.dc:creator: Juan Diego Mazo-V\'asquez, Lewis Hill, Flore K. Kunst, Gian-Luca Oppo

item.title: Selection of Marginally Stable Patterns by Boundary Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15201v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the effect of boundary conditions on the selection of wavenumbers in pattern-forming systems. Prior work established that, for a large class of boundary conditions, equilibria only within a narrow band of wavenumbers are compatible with the boundary. We demonstrate here that for a large class of initial conditions, solutions evolve towards an extremal member of this narrow band of equilibria. In fact, this extremal member is linearly stable, nonlinearly unstable, and the convergence is realized through a series of snapping events at the boundary. We observe this behavior in simulations of the Swift-Hohenberg equation when the pattern forming region is confined to a large spatial interval through a parameter quench. We prove the convergence in a phase-diffusion approximation using comparison principles and astutely chosen subsolutions that mimic the snapping behavior.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Daniels, Simon Eskin, Tel Fahrendholz, Arnd Scheel
